The change adds a clock-and-sleep parameter pair defaulting to the real functions to two mobile runner modules (a SettleWaiter seam), routes 23 unconditional settle calls on 21 lines through it while leaving the two condition waits in the android driver class raw (stop_recording's time.sleep(1) flush wait and wait_boot's time.sleep(2) boot poll, one call each, both measured unchanged against 84e9233 by AST), and adds the selftest block that asserts the resolved pair, the requested durations and their order, re-synced byte-identical across plugin/templates and all six packs. evidence.ref: THE ASSERTION NOW BINDS THE RUNNER'S OWN RESOLUTION, WHICH IS THE FINDING THAT FAILED ROUND 1. Both mobile runners define an identical `SettleWaiter` with `__init__(self, clock=time.monotonic, sleep=time.sleep, record=None)` and ONE public method, `settle(seconds, reason)`. ROUND 1 ASSERTED THE IDENTITY ON A SettleWaiter THE SUITE BUILT ITSELF, which establishes the class default and says nothing about what the runner resolves. RE-MEASURED IN THIS ROUND, not taken on trust from the review: with `SettleWaiter()` replaced by `SettleWaiter(sleep=lambda s: None)` at every resolution site of all seven tracked android copies, round 1's assertion set reported `selftest: 3261 passed, 0 failed` and exited 0. Adopter waiting was gone and nothing reddened. WHAT REPLACES IT: `_v13_runner_resolutions` execs each tracked copy into a fresh namespace, replaces SettleWaiter with a subclass whose `__init__` DELEGATES to the shipped one (so the resolution observed is the shipped resolution) and whose `settle` is a no-op (so exercising a production-path site costs no wall time), then DRIVES every resolution site the module's own AST declares with the waiter argument OMITTED and asserts, by identity, that the waiter THE RUNNER CONSTRUCTED has `_sleep is time.sleep`, `_clock is time.monotonic` and `_record is None`. The site set is DERIVED: `_v13_resolution_sites` walks every `SettleWaiter(...)` Call to its innermost enclosing FunctionDef, so nothing names run, apply_step or redrive to FIND a site, and the assertion demands set equality between the derived sites and the exercise table, so a fourth resolution site added tomorrow reddens the gate until it is covered rather than going quietly unexercised.

THE FIX IS PROVEN BY DRIVING THE EXACT MUTATION, THREE WAYS, ACROSS ALL SEVEN COPIES. (1) IN-SUITE, PER SITE: for every tracked copy of both runners and every SettleWaiter construction in it, one at a time, an AST mutant that gives THAT ONE construction `sleep=lambda s: None` is REFUSED. 42 mutants (7 copies x 3 constructions x 2 runners, the counts DERIVED from git ls-files and the AST on every run, never typed); not one survives. (2) IN-SUITE, THE REVIEWER'S LITERAL TEXT EDIT: `SettleWaiter()` replaced by `SettleWaiter(sleep=lambda s: None)` in every tracked copy is refused in all 14, and the number of text hits is asserted equal to the AST-derived construction count so the mutation cannot be silently matching nothing. (3) ON DISK, THE WHOLE GATE: the same text edit written into all SEVEN android copies and the FULL suite run reports `selftest: 3259 passed, 4 failed` and exits 1, reddening AC1, the reviewer's-exact-edit control (whose text no longer applies), the production-path no-leak control and the injection-site control, with the files then restored by `git checkout --` and re-verified byte-identical (sha256 eb429a8e92798074b9cf3aafdeed7f4bcaabb39f85df9036cced72be2cc0bd63). The mutant generator REPLACES an existing sleep keyword instead of appending a second one, because the first attempt at demonstration (3) raised `SyntaxError: keyword argument repeated: sleep` and a traceback with no `selftest: N passed` line makes a run that found the defect indistinguishable from a run that found nothing.

THE CLOCK PARAMETER EARNS ITS PLACE RATHER THAN SHIPPING UNUSED. Nothing on the production path reads it: `settle` tests one attribute against None and calls sleep, so a production settle never touches the clock at all. On the RECORDING path it timestamps each settle, and the gate asserts `t1 - t0 == seconds` for every recorded entry AND that the virtual now equals the running sum of requested seconds, which proves the seam neither slept twice for one settle nor timestamped one settle with another settle's reading. ROUND 1 ALSO CALLED THIS A LEAK DETECTOR THAT PROVED THE RUNNER'S TIME CAME FROM THE INJECTED PAIR AND NOWHERE ELSE, AND THAT SENTENCE IS DELETED: the assertion ranges only over entries the recorder was handed, so it cannot see time that escaped to the real module. The escape claim now belongs to the c_call observer under AC3, which was measured able to see it.

THE PARAMETER IS THREADED AS A TRAILING DEFAULTED ARGUMENT through run / apply_step / redrive, so no existing signature moves and every existing call keeps working; the recording hook stays in the gate and no fake clock ships. The seam is the house pattern already at .warp/fleet.py (clock=time.time, sleep=time.sleep) and .warp/tracker_mirror_runner.py, applied to two modules written without it. AC1's own criterion text was AMENDED ON THE RECORD in this round because its original wording (a selftest that constructs each RUNNER with no arguments) was satisfiable, and was satisfied, without closing the risk; a dogfood assertion reads the amended text and refuses the old sentence, so a criterion a build can satisfy while leaving the hole open cannot read as satisfied.

THE CRITERION'S OWN COUNT WAS MEASURED FALSE IN ROUND 1 AND IS AMENDED ON THE RECORD, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS REPEATED HERE FROM GIT RATHER THAN CARRIED OVER. `git show 84e9233:<path> | grep -c 'time\.sleep'` counts LINES; `| grep -o 'time\.sleep' | wc -l` counts CALLS. Measured again in this round: warp_android_runner.py 12 lines / 15 calls, warp_ios_runner.py 9 lines / 10 calls, with android lines 190, 204 and 206 and iOS line 222 each carrying TWO calls. So 25 calls, of which 23 are unconditional settles and 2 are condition waits. AC2 reads 23 ROUTED CALLS ON 21 LINES and NAMES the two left raw. proof/WARP-0711/baseline.md carries the same LINE counts and is a frozen historical record, so it is left alone. A dogfood assertion reads the amended AC2 text, so a criterion left stating a false count cannot read as satisfied.

THREE-WAY CONSTANT EQUALITY, EACH SIDE PRODUCED BY A DIFFERENT MECHANISM, over all 23 constants. (1) A FROZEN 23-entry table in the selftest, which IS the criterion text a reviewer reads. (2) A map PARSED out of each shipped module's AST, with the literal recovered from a bare Constant or from the default of `step.get(..., <Constant>)`. (3) A map OBSERVED by the recorder while driving both runners against the existing fake drivers with fixtures that override NOTHING, so what is observed IS the shipped default. All three asserted EQUAL. The values: android launch 2, tap 1, text 0.5, key 0.5, wait 1, rotation 1 and 1, process_death 1 then 2, background_foreground 1 then 2, network_loss 1 and 1 (13); iOS launch 2, tap 1, type 0.5, wait 1, process_death 1 then 2, background_foreground 1 then 2, appearance 1 and 1 (10). That mutant is the shortcut AC2 forbids, demonstrated as a gate failure rather than promised as a discipline.

THE CONSTANTS ARE RE-PROVEN AGAINST THE PARENT REVISION BY AST, INDEPENDENTLY OF THE SUITE, because the review's one piece of good news has to survive this rework. A standalone script reads BOTH revisions out of `git show` (never the worktree, so an edited file cannot fool it) and reduces every duration expression to a comparable value, with `step.get("settle", 2)` reduced to ("override", "settle", 2) so a port that dropped an override cannot compare equal to one that kept it. AN ADOPTER'S DECLARED WINDOW STILL WINS. No duration was hoisted to a named constant: `time.sleep(step.get("settle", 2))` became `waiter.settle(step.get("settle", 2), "launch")`, the smallest diff that leaves the one thing AC2 asks a reviewer to confirm readable. PROVEN ABLE TO FIRE: dropping the `step.get` and hardcoding the default (the port mistake that would silently ignore every adopter's declared window while every constant assertion stayed green) turns it RED.

THE WAITS ARE NOW ASSERTED BEHAVIOUR, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE ITEM. Before this change the gate established exactly one thing about a settle: that time passed. Now, for one all-sites journey per module, the RECORDED (reason, seconds) sequence is asserted EQUAL to the expected sequence, in ORDER, including process_death recording terminate-then-launch IN THAT ORDER as an explicit slice on top of the whole-sequence equality. The fixtures reach tap, text, key, type and wait, which the gate's own journeys never exercised, so this is new coverage and not only recovered time. COMPLETENESS is asserted in BOTH directions with both sides DERIVED: the set of settle reasons in the module AST EQUALS the set the recorder observed, and labels are asserted UNIQUE within each module because two sites sharing a label would collapse two waits into one in every order assertion. PROVEN ABLE TO FIRE: swapping the two network_loss settles reddens the ORDER assertion while completeness stays green, which is the discrimination durations alone cannot give (1 appears eight times and 2 five times across the 23).

THE NO-REAL-SLEEP PROBE NOW OBSERVES WHAT IS ACTUALLY CALLED, WHICH IS THE SECOND FINDING THAT FAILED ROUND 1. Round 1 swapped the `time.sleep` MODULE ATTRIBUTE, but `SettleWaiter.__init__` binds the real sleep at DEF time to the function OBJECT, so a production-path settle calls that object directly and the wrapper could never fire. RE-MEASURED IN THIS ROUND: a SettleWaiter built with defaults, with the module-attribute wrapper installed, and `settle(0, "launch")` called, fires the wrapper ZERO times (measured, empty list). THE REPLACEMENT observes the CALL and not the attribute: a `sys.setprofile` hook reads `c_call` events, whose arg IS the callee object, so `arg is time.sleep` sees every real sleep however it was bound, attributed to the CALLER's module through the frame. The same construction under the new observer is charged exactly one sleep to `warp_android_probe`. The observer is installed only for the windows this block opens and removed in a `finally`, so a failure inside a probed run cannot leave the suite instrumented. ASSERTED: across both all-sites runs, ZERO real sleeps are charged to either mobile runner module. Zero is the invariant; it is not a count of anything in this repository.

THE PROBE'S NEGATIVE CONTROL IS ADDITIVE AND REACHES THE PATH THE OLD ONE COULD NOT. Round 1's control was a two-line source whose `__name__` begins with warp_android calling `time.sleep(0)` through the time module; it is kept and still charges EXACTLY ONE, but round 1's conclusion from it, that the zero was therefore a measurement and not a wrapper that never fires, IS DELETED, because the path it exercised is not the path the guard exists for. THE ADDED CONTROL: a fresh copy of each shipped runner is driven with the waiter argument OMITTED on a journey whose every declared window is ZERO, so the runner resolves its own REAL waiter and really calls `time.sleep`, twice, for no seconds; the observer must charge exactly ["warp_android_prodpath", "warp_android_prodpath"] and the iOS equivalent. It ADDS a drive site rather than renaming one, which is the shape a growth blind spot hides in, and it is one of the four assertions the on-disk mutation reddens.

THE REPLACEMENT OBSERVES THE PROPERTY instead of describing it: `_mw_instrument`, installed beside each runner's load, replaces the loaded module's SettleWaiter with a subclass that delegates `__init__` and records every construction with the CALLER's module name from the frame. Two facts are then asserted over whatever the gate actually did, in any call form, named or not, existing or added tomorrow: no waiter was resolved BY A RUNNER ITSELF, and not one waiter built through either loaded runner carries the real `time.sleep` (which also catches a drive site that hands over an explicitly real-clock waiter, a shape the AST check never covered). THE SAVING IS STILL NOT MEASURED, AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATUS OF AC4 RATHER THAN A GAP DISCOVERED LATER. Measured with `pgrep -c -f 'python3 scripts/selftest.py'` while this round was built: SIX concurrent selftest processes from sibling worktrees on this machine, with a one-minute load average of 0.79 at the start of the session. This round's own child run took 146.7s wall for 62.9s of user time, which is a contention ratio and not a gate time. A wall-clock A/B taken here would be published and then refuted. What IS published is a DERIVATION, labelled as one: the DETERMINISTIC SUM of the settle seconds the gate's mobile drive sites REQUEST, collected by the injected waiter and printed by the gate, is 46.0 seconds across 31 waits. It agrees with the independently measured cumtimes in proof/WARP-0711/baseline.md (warp_android_runner.py:run 24.006s over 5 calls, warp_ios_runner.py:run 22.010s over 5 calls; 24.0 + 22.0 = 46.0), which is the one corroboration available without measuring. THIS PROXY IS BLIND TO: real sleep overhead and scheduler granularity (so the true saving is slightly LARGER than the sum, never smaller); anything else in the suite that changes at the same commit; and the possibility that a real machine measures differently. AC4 binds to the MEASURED number, so if M1 returns a delta smaller than 46 the manifest states the measured figure and 46 is deleted.

THE QUIESCENCE PREMISE IS PROVEN AROUND THIS ITEM'S FIXTURES, NOT AROUND EVERY MOBILE PATH. During the probed runs an audit hook asserts ZERO agent-creating events (subprocess.Popen, os.fork, os.exec, os.system, os.posix_spawn, _thread.start_new_thread, socket.connect, socket.getaddrinfo) and an UNCHANGED live thread count (compared to itself, never to a literal), with a negative control that starts and joins one thread inside the window and is reported. Site coverage is complete because the AST and recorder site sets must be EQUAL, but coverage of sites is not coverage of driver SUBCLASSES: if a future fake driver gains a thread on a path only the two early blocks reach, the hook never sees it.

THE INJECTION-SITE OBSERVATION COVERS DRIVE SITES THAT EXECUTE. A drive site behind a condition that does not run in a given gate is not observed. That is sound for the property it guards, since a site that does not run pays no gate time, but it is a narrower claim than the AST check it replaces pretended to make: a drive site added inside a branch nothing reaches stays invisible until it runs.

THE EQUIVALENCE DIFFERENTIAL RUNS AT 0.02 OF EACH CONSTANT (about 0.55 real seconds for both modules), so it can only see a latent time dependence whose threshold is under 2 percent of the constant, 40ms for a 2s launch settle. Running it at full length would eat more than half the saving forever in the item whose purpose is removing that time. Its sensitivity is DEMONSTRATED rather than claimed: a planted load-bearing wait (a driver whose focus settles only 0.01 real seconds after the launch) makes the real arm PASS and the virtual arm FAIL. It is corroboration; the quiescence argument is the proof.

THE PRODUCTION FAST PATH IS EXERCISED BY THREE THINGS AND NONE OF THEM IS AN ADOPTER'S REAL DEVICE: the differential's real-sleeping arm, the two zero-window production-path probes, and the AC1 resolution drives (which delegate __init__ but stub settle). A bug reachable only in the fast path with a NON-zero duration on real hardware would still be invisible here.

A CONSTANT CHANGED IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE FROZEN TABLE IS NOT CAUGHT BY THE THREE-WAY EQUALITY, because the AST, the table and the recorder all move together if a builder edits the table to match. The defence is that the table IS the criterion text a reviewer reads, the same numbers appear in AC2, and the standalone AST re-proof compares against the PARENT REVISION out of git, which a table edit cannot move.

THE SEAM'S {settle}-ONLY API, THE NO-SETTLE-IN-A-LOOP RULE AND THE AC1 EXERCISE TABLE ARE CHECKS A LATER ITEM MUST ARGUE PAST TO GENERALIZE THE SEAM. Nothing but review catches a deliberate edit to a check itself, including deleting an entry from the exercise table together with the resolution site it covered.

WARP-0712 IS THE DEPENDENCY THAT COULD FORCE A REDESIGN RATHER THAN AN EDIT. If it splits scripts/selftest.py into modules or runs blocks in PARALLEL, the injection-site observation has to be reconciled across workers and parallelism would break the quiescence premise outright: a worker beside the mobile runs makes the thread count unstable and puts a real agent of change in the process. The probe would correctly go RED, which is the right outcome.

WARP-0715 OWNS THE FROZEN PROCESS-RUNNER DIGEST. If it lands first the digest is stale and this gate goes red on an unrelated item until it is updated. Accepted deliberately, with the alternative being that generalizing the seam into the process runner becomes a review finding instead of a gate failure.

THE INJECTION-SITE OBSERVATION IS INSTALLED ON THE TWO LOADED RUNNER MODULES. A drive that execs a FRESH copy of a runner's source is not instrumented by it and could pay wall time invisibly. This block itself does exactly that, four times, always on zero-window journeys, and the c_call observer covers those windows; a future block doing it on a full-length journey would not be caught by either guard.

THE RESOLUTION-SITE DERIVATION FINDS `SettleWaiter(...)` BY THAT NAME IN THE MODULE'S OWN AST. A resolution written indirectly (through globals(), a factory, or an alias) would not be discovered, so the exercise-table equality could not demand a recipe for it and the runner-resolution assertion would not reach it. Nothing but review catches that shape.

sys.setprofile IS PROCESS-WIDE AND PER-THREAD. It is installed only for the windows this block opens and removed in a finally, but a future block that installs its own profiler around a mobile drive would silently displace this observer, and nothing asserts that no other profiler is installed.

THE BATTERY IS A BUILDER-RUN ARTIFACT, NOT A GATE STAGE. Its six runs are recorded here and reproducible from the script, but nothing in scripts/verify.sh re-runs them, so a later change that reopens one of those holes would not be caught by the battery, only by the in-suite assertions it exercised.
